mirror_verdict.claim: The M1 sky is a mirror image of the real sky: Starfield.galactic_to_world is a reflection (det -1); facing the galactic centre with the NGP up, l = 90 deg appears on the right instead of the left.
evidence: 1. Determinant: galactic_to_world(x, y, z) = (y, z, -x) (sky/starfield.gd:31-32) is the matrix [[0,1,0],[0,0,1],[-1,0,0]]; det = -1 (evaluator's Python; also Basis(...).determinant() = -1.000000 in a headless Godot probe). The rotation candidate (-y, z, -x) has det +1.

2. Handedness oracle (Python, right-handed galactic frame, observer at the origin, right = forward x up): facing the GC with the NGP up, Antares (l 351.95) and alpha Cen A (l 315.73) are on the RIGHT in the real sky; through the M1 mapping, a Godot camera (right = forward x up in Godot's own right-handed world) puts them on the LEFT. Facing Crux: alpha Cen A real LEFT, M1 RIGHT; the LMC real RIGHT, M1 LEFT. Facing Orion's belt: Alnitak (l 206.45) real LEFT of Alnilam, M1 RIGHT; Mintaka (l 203.86) real RIGHT, M1 LEFT. Every off-axis star swaps side.

3. In-engine projection (headless Godot, a real Camera3D looking along galactic_to_world(+x) with up galactic_to_world(+z), 960 px wide): Antares screen x 412 (LEFT; real: right), alpha Cen A x 12 (LEFT; real: right), the Scutum cloud l 25 x 704 (RIGHT; real: left), Vega l 67 x 1636 (RIGHT; real: left).

4. M1 captures (make capture re-run here with the NOIRLab background, contrast-stretched by the evaluator): in sky_b00_starboard.png (the camera looking along Godot +X = l 90, Cygnus, north up) M31 (l 121, b -21.6) renders at about (710, 450) of 960x540, i.e. ~31 deg RIGHT of centre and ~22 deg down; in the real sky, with galactic north up, l 121 is 31 deg to the LEFT of l 90. In sky_b00_port.png (Godot -X = l 270, Vela) the LMC (l 280.5, b -33) renders right of centre at about (540, 510); in the real sky it is 10 deg to the LEFT of l 270. The Gum nebula (l 263) renders left of centre; really it is right. Also: M1's 'port' view looks at l 270, but the port side of a ship facing the galactic centre with north up is l 90 in the real sky.

5. GPU gate: with the PR's flip (SKY_FLIP_H true) G-M4-1 lands 72/72 star positions within 0.159 px of the right-handed cam_bridge.json projection; the evaluator's mutation SKY_FLIP_H = false fails 72/72 with worst 606 px (the stars render on the mirrored column). The same mutation fails test_interior's det/flip coupling check (2 failures), as does making galactic_to_world a rotation while the flip stays on.
mirror_verdict.catalogue_context: PR #37 (merged 2026-10-02) fixed a different, data-side mirror: process_stars.sh had l_cat = 245.86 - l_true, verified against SIMBAD/astropy for 16 stars; stars.json is now IAU-correct (positive y toward l 90). PR #37's note that 'sky/starfield.gd, sky/background.gdshader, sky/sky_model.gd and tools/m14a_register.py all use the same convention' is true, and that is exactly why the whole M1 sky (stars + panorama + CMB) is one consistent mirror image: the catalogue is right, the panorama registration is right, and the single galactic->Godot map reflects all of them together. It was invisible to every M1 gate because every golden compares the GPU with a CPU reference that goes through the same map, and PR #37's panorama overlays were checked in image space, not in-engine.
mirror_verdict.local_correction_consistent: Yes, and exact. Derivation: with M orthogonal and det M = -1, a camera built from f' = Mf, u' = Mu has right r' = f' x u' = -Mr, so a direction d' = Md projects to (-d.r, d.u, d.f): the render is the exact horizontal mirror of the true view, and flip_h restores it pixel for pixel because the view region is symmetric about the centre column. Aberration and Doppler depend only on angles between d and v, which M preserves; the glow shader forms ship-frame components by dot products with the mapped axes, which M also preserves; and G-M4-4 (c) indexes the texture column W-1-x. So the interior's starfield, panorama, CMB and glow are all correctly handed; G-M4-1 proves it on the GPU.
mirror_verdict.fixing_m1_entails: Make the map a rotation in one place (e.g. galactic_to_world(g) = (-g.y, g.z, -g.x), inverse world->galactic (-z, x, -y)) and remove the hand copies: sky/starfield.gd:31, sky/sky_model.gd:30, sky/background.gdshader:60 (and the u = 0.5 - atan(y,x)/TAU sampling stays, since it is the panorama's own l convention), interior/interior_sky.gd:138/:168/:196, interior/interior_smoke.gd:91, tools/interior_golden.gd:89/:114, main.gd:734, tests/test_physics.gd:297, spike/panorama_main.gd:53, tools/m14a_register.py if it feeds engine coordinates; then SKY_FLIP_H = false and the G-M4-4 (c) column index. Goldens: every GPU-vs-CPU golden (M1.6b 144 off-axis + 16 markers, stand-off, exposure, CMB, G-M4-1..4) should stay green because both sides share the map, but any golden or test with hard-coded screen positions, yaw signs (e.g. the 'port'/'starboard' labels and KEY_1-4 views in main.gd, FreeLookCamera yaw conventions), or pinned PNG references will change; test_ship_frame's camera-projection check values in tests/test_physics.gd:850 need re-deriving only if they pass through the map. Renders: every reference render in renders/ (M1 captures, exposure_sheet, cmb_sheet, M2.6 map captures, the interior captures) becomes its mirror image and must be regenerated and looked at (gate 2); docs/ overlays from PR #37 are image-space and unaffected. The galaxy map (ui/galaxy_map.gd:408/:731/:840) also uses the map for star positions, so its orbit/ring and the pinned map captures flip too. Recommend one dedicated PR with before/after contact sheets, raised to Mark as a ledger decision (the interior's local flip is then removed in the same PR).

glow_physics_verdict.profile: Correct and pinned: pole x clamp(cos theta, 0, 1) is glowEmittanceAt's shape; the pole is the sim's number (absent today). Recomputed from first principles with CODATA m_p c^2 and c: K(0.99c) = 1.9258e5 W/m^2, glow_w_m2 = eps f_in K / 4 = 2.4072e-5, pole = 9.6288e-5; at 1 - beta = 1e-6: gamma 707.107, K 2.2502e9, glow_w_m2 0.28127, pole 1.12508. All match the package probe (VM = interpreter, identical) and the test constants.
glow_physics_verdict.lambertian: E/pi is the right radiance for a Lambertian emitter of exitance E (L = M/pi); the overlay then shows the WALL POINT's emittance along each ray from the off-centre camera, which is physically the right quantity (not the view direction's cos). Verified: wall_cos for the bridge camera (16, -8, 83.7) straight up = sqrt(100^2 - 16^2 - 8^2)/100 = 0.98387, sideways = 0.837; G-M4-4 (c) 0.089 % on six off-centre pixels.
glow_physics_verdict.efficacy: 182.5654 lm/W = 683 x (trapezoid sum of ybar at 1 nm over 380-780) / 400 reproduces exactly from the Wyman-Sloan-Shirley 2013 multi-lobe fit (the package's cmf is that fit). The CIE 1931 tabulated integral (106.857 nm) gives 182.46 lm/W, 0.06 % lower: fine for a placeholder and inside the 1 % golden. The colour WHITE_RGB is illuminant E in linear sRGB with Y = 1.0000001. It IS a placeholder: higgs-bubble.md gives no spectrum, and the number moves by up to x3.7 with the spectrum (a 2700 K blackbody is ~50 lm/W; 5800 K ~93 lm/W), so Mark's ruling changes the brightness by that factor, not the chain.
glow_physics_verdict.exposure: pixel = E/pi x lm/W x k, k = 1/L_white(EV) the same linear-pixel-per-cd/m^2 the stars and the background use (Exposure.k()); no gain. G-M4-4 (d) 0.09338 vs 0.09342 (0.04 %). The glow is in the eye meter, so the dark-adapted eye light-adapts to it (EV -4.40 at 0.99c, +9.17 at the cap), which is honest.
glow_physics_verdict.pole_at_eps_1e-9_vs_dark_sky: Recomputed: L = 9.6288e-5 / pi x 182.565 = 5.5955e-3 cd/m^2. The repo's dark sky is 23.5 mag/arcsec^2 (Exposure.DARK_SKY_MAG, the deep-space value) = 4.30e-5 cd/m^2, so the ratio is 130.1: the executor's ~130x is right. Against a 22.0 mag/arcsec^2 ground dark site it is 33x; against the brightest Milky Way patches (~20 mag/arcsec^2, 1.08e-3 cd/m^2) still 5x. It is a mesopic 5.6e-3 cd/m^2 wall, not faint, and it does wash out the starfield (capture 10). This is not an M4.2 defect: the chain is exactly what the design asked for, and the design's 'faint by design (eps = 1e-9)' sentence is what is wrong. To be faint relative to the Milky Way the pole would need eps of order 1e-11 (or f_in much below 0.5, or a dim spectrum). Needs a ruling (eps, f_in, spectrum, or accept); the HB-61 bound (<= 1 W/m^2 at the cap) is not a faintness bound.
glow_physics_verdict.verdict: PASS on gate 2 for the overlay as a mirror of the package profile and the one shared exposure. Open items for Mark: the spectrum (placeholder), eps/f_in (not faint), and the gate-3 follow-up (E/pi and efficacy into the package once the spectrum is ruled).
